title: Greenwood Village
name: Greenwood Village
metaDescription: Greenwood Village 1031 exchange coordination for institutional-grade office and high-end retail near the Denver Tech Center, where boot exposure runs higher than average.

sections.html: Greenwood Village trades at a different price point than almost anywhere else in the metro. The corporate campuses along I-25 and the Denver Tech Center's southern edge bring in buyers who move slower and ask harder questions than a typical retail buyer would, and a seller here needs an exchange team that can match that pace.

sections.heading: Corporate Campuses Set the Tone
sections.html: Large single- and multi-tenant office buildings along Orchard Road and the I-25 corridor have anchored Greenwood Village for decades, drawing corporate tenants that lease long and pay well. That history shapes buyer expectations here, an investor underwriting a Greenwood Village office building is usually comparing it against other institutional-grade product, not a typical suburban office park, and pricing reflects that comparison set. The city's residential zoning is also unusually restrictive for a Denver suburb, which has kept a hard line between the corporate corridor and the surrounding neighborhoods rather than letting the two blend together the way they have in some nearby submarkets.

sections.heading: What Actually Trades
sections.html:
Institutional-quality office near Orchard Road and the DTC's southern edge makes up the bulk of exchange volume. High-end retail and restaurant space serving the corporate workforce trades less often but commands strong pricing when it does. Multifamily near the light rail stations has grown as more of the workforce looks to live close to the campuses, and rents there have held up even through periods when the broader metro's apartment market has softened, largely because the tenant base skews toward stable corporate salaries rather than more cyclical industries. Categories worth tracking:

  • Institutional-grade office along Orchard Road and the DTC's southern edge
  • High-end retail and restaurant space serving the corporate workforce
  • Multifamily near the Orchard and Arapahoe light rail stations
  • Medical office serving the surrounding affluent population
  • DST interests for owners scaling down from direct office ownership

sections.heading: Boot Math Matters More at This Price Point
sections.html: Because Greenwood Village office trades at institutional pricing, a seller moving into a smaller or lower-leverage replacement can trigger real taxable boot without realizing it until the numbers are run. I walk through that math with every seller before they get attached to a specific replacement candidate, since the dollar amounts here are large enough that a miscalculation is expensive. Debt relief on the relinquished property is frequently the overlooked piece of that calculation.

sections.heading: The Qualified Intermediary Earns Their Fee Here
sections.html: A Greenwood Village deal usually involves more parties, lenders, corporate legal teams, sometimes an institutional seller on the other side of the transaction, so the qualified intermediary's coordination role matters more than in a simpler retail exchange. Documentation needs to be airtight given the values involved, and I've seen a sloppy assignment agreement create real headaches at closing on a deal this size, headaches that a more careful intake process would have avoided entirely. Even a minor drafting error on an assignment can force a delay while an institutional counterparty's legal team reviews and re-approves it.

sections.heading: What Slows These Deals Down
sections.html: Corporate sellers and buyers here move at institutional speed, which is sometimes slower than a typical retail closing. Lease abstracts, tenant estoppels, and title work take longer on large single-tenant buildings. I tell sellers to build extra time into their identification and closing schedule rather than assuming a Greenwood Village deal will move at the pace of a strip mall sale, since it rarely does. A corporate legal department reviewing a tenant estoppel can add real weeks a smaller deal simply wouldn't have to absorb, and that timeline should be built into the closing schedule from the start rather than discovered midway through.

faqs.q: Why does boot come up more often in Greenwood Village exchanges?
faqs.a: Institutional-grade office here trades at a high price point, so a seller moving into a lower-value or lower-leverage replacement can end up with taxable boot without planning for it. Running that math early avoids a surprise at closing, and debt relief is often the piece a seller overlooks entirely.

faqs.q: Does the qualified intermediary do more work on a Greenwood Village deal?
faqs.a: The coordination role is bigger when lenders, corporate legal teams, or institutional sellers are involved, which is common here. Documentation needs to be thorough given the values at stake, and a sloppy assignment agreement can create real problems at closing.

faqs.q: Why do Greenwood Village office deals close slower than retail exchanges?
faqs.a: Lease abstracts, tenant estoppels, and title work take longer on large single-tenant institutional buildings. Building extra time into the closing schedule avoids pressure against the 180-day deadline, since these deals rarely move at retail speed and a corporate legal department can add weeks on its own.

faqs.q: Is multifamily near the light rail stations a good replacement for Greenwood Village office?
faqs.a: It can be for an investor looking to diversify out of office risk, since like-kind rules allow that shift as long as both properties are real property held for investment. It also reduces exposure to any single corporate tenant, which is a real consideration coming out of an institutional office sale.

faqs.q: Can 1031 Exchange Denver negotiate my Greenwood Village office sale?
faqs.a: No. This service coordinates identification, scheduling, and communication among the investor's own broker, lender, and qualified intermediary. Negotiating the transaction itself is handled by the investor's broker and legal counsel, and any tax position is confirmed by the investor's CPA.
